title: Module 24: Staying in Touch — Communication Apps

screens.heading: You are safe here
screens.reassurance: This module will not send any messages or make any calls. You are just reading.
screens.goal: By the end of this module, you will understand the main ways to communicate digitally — calls, texts, video, and messaging apps — and know which ones work best for staying close to the people who matter most.

screens.heading: Dorothy's missed calls
body: Dorothy, 73, had a pattern: she would think of her daughter in the afternoon, decide it was probably not a good time to call, and not call. Her daughter would think of her mother in the evening, decide she was probably asleep, and not call. Weeks would pass.
Neither of them was avoiding the other. They were both waiting for the perfect moment — which never came.

Technology gave Dorothy and her daughter a solution: a standing 'Good morning' text every day. Takes 5 seconds. Confirms both are okay. And when one does not arrive, the other calls immediately. The small habit replaced the worry.
screens.tellMeMore: The most important insight about communication technology: it is only useful if it fits your actual habits and relationships. The best communication tool is not the most sophisticated one — it is the one you will actually use. Start with what feels most natural and comfortable.

screens.heading: Voice calls — the familiar one
body: A regular phone call remains one of the most personal and comfortable ways to connect. Your voice carries warmth, humour, and emotion that text cannot replicate.

On iPhone: tap the Phone app (green icon). Tap 'Contacts' to find someone or tap the keypad to dial a number. To call through Wi-Fi (no cell signal needed): FaceTime Audio — open FaceTime, tap the + button, search for the person, and tap the phone icon.
On Android: tap the Phone app. Tap 'Contacts' or dial directly. Google Duo and WhatsApp also offer free voice calls over Wi-Fi — useful when you have no cell signal but have Wi-Fi.
screens.tellMeMore: If you find phone calls tiring because of hearing difficulties, consider captioned phone calls. The Hamilton CapTel service in Canada provides phones that display a text caption of everything the other person says in real time — free for eligible Canadians with hearing loss. Visit hamiltoncaptel.ca for details.

screens.heading: Text messages and messaging apps
body: Text messages are perfect for quick, low-pressure connection: a photo of the sunset, a funny thought, 'Thinking of you.' The recipient reads it when convenient — no one needs to be available at the same time.

Standard SMS (the green bubble on iPhone) works on any phone. iMessage (blue bubble) works between Apple devices and is free over Wi-Fi. WhatsApp is the most popular cross-platform messaging app — used by families worldwide because it works on any device and is free.

WhatsApp setup: download from the App Store or Google Play, create a free account with your phone number. Start a conversation by tapping the compose button and searching for a contact. Your whole family can join a group chat in minutes.
screens.tellMeMore: WhatsApp voice notes are a favourite feature for many seniors. Instead of typing a long message, press and hold the microphone button, speak your message, and release. The recipient hears your voice — more personal than text, less demanding than a phone call. It is also perfect if typing is difficult due to arthritis or tremor.

screens.heading: Messaging apps for different relationships
body: WhatsApp: ideal for international family, group chats with multiple family members across different devices. Free, encrypted, widely used globally.
Facebook Messenger: good if your family is already on Facebook. Handles voice calls, video calls, and text. Works on any device.
iMessage (built into iPhone/iPad): seamless, no setup required, excellent for families where everyone uses Apple. Includes features like Memoji, shared photos, and reactions.
Email: best for longer, more formal messages — sharing documents, photos, newsletters. Less immediate than messaging apps but more permanent.
screens.tellMeMore: There is no need to choose one and stick to it exclusively. Many families use different tools for different purposes: WhatsApp for quick messages, email for sharing photos, FaceTime for video calls. The key is knowing what each tool does well and using the one that suits the moment.

screens.heading: Staying connected is easier than waiting for the perfect moment
takeaways: A simple daily habit — like a good morning text — replaces worry with reassurance for both sides.
Voice calls carry warmth that text cannot. FaceTime Audio and WhatsApp calls are free over Wi-Fi.
WhatsApp works on any device (iPhone and Android) and is free — the most practical choice for mixed-device families.
WhatsApp voice notes let you speak a message instead of typing — perfect if typing is difficult.
There is no single best app — use whatever your family is comfortable with and will actually use.
screens.confidence: You now know the full toolkit for staying in touch with family — and a simple daily habit that makes distance feel much smaller.
